doc.title: Jane Monheit interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 20, 2010

title: Audience rapport, venues and singing from her iPhone
summary: She acts the same in any venue, aims for laughter and tears, and reads lyrics from her phone in small clubs.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Well that’s a good answer. When you go out to do a show does it matter — that’s not really the right word — if you know that your show is going to be in a club with a maximum capacity of 125 as opposed to a 2500 theater that you hope to fill, does it change your choice of material?

Nope. Not at all. And It doesn’t change the way I conduct myself on stage either. What will change the way I conduct myself is the level of formality. I might be a little bit different at a very formal affair with a full orchestra, say the orchestra is in tuxes and I’m in a gown, I might not be cracking so many jokes and being quite as silly. Because I really like to make people laugh and I try and it often doesn’t work but for me the perfect show is if there’s some kind of catharsis where everybody laughs and cries. I do, in every show. When they start applauding sometimes I crack up because it’s just like you’re clapping for us. Or if I’m singing a ballad I’ll totally choke up and cry. And I want them to do that too. But yeah, no I really act the same everywhere I go. I didn’t used to. I used to think I had to behave a certain way and be really fake and say certain things and be this image of this perfect jazz princess, and I cut that loose a while ago.

Well I noticed your relationship with the audience, I saw you perform at The Other Side in Utica, which was 60 people maximum almost, and it was nice, it was homey, and I cracked up when someone asked you a question about a song and you said, “Wait a minute” and you whipped out your —

Oh my iPhone. I’ve done that in clubs. I’ve been like I really want to sing this but I can’t remember the words. I swear I know the melody to like seven thousand songs and I don’t know the words to any of them. So I will pull out my phone and read lyrics. I’ve done it. I mean I wouldn’t do it at a big fancy gig, but in a little club where everything is super loose, loose enough that I can wear jeans, I’ll pull out my phone.
Okay. If it’s a jean gig out comes the phone.

But only for lyrics on a tune that I really really want to do or if it’s something somebody requested, or I’ll have my phone on stage for New Year’s Eve gigs so I know when it’s going to be midnight, and otherwise no.
Oh right, you don’t want to miss the ball coming down.
